sections.content:
Population change in South Norfolk in 2032

The population in South Norfolk is projected to increase from 144,617 people in 2022 to 166,982 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net internal migration, which will increase the population by 24,639 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in South Norfolk
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In South Norfolk, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More deaths than births mean that the population is projected to decrease by 3,599, with 12,834 births and 16,433 deaths in South Norfolk between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would decrease the population in South Norfolk by 2.5%, compared with an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to increase the population by 24,639, with 115,301 people moving to the area and 90,662 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in South Norfolk by 17.0%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 269, with 1,534 people moving to the area and 1,803 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in South Norfolk by 0.2%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 1,628, with 5,420 people moving to the area and 3,792 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in South Norfolk by 1.1%, compared with an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in South Norfolk in 2032

The median age in South Norfolk is projected to rise from 46 years in 2022 to 47 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 25% of the population in South Norfolk are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 23% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in South Norfolk between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in South Norfolk is projected to stay the same, at around 59%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 392 to 396 over the same time period.

This is above average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in South Norfolk?

In 2032, 19% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 21% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in South Norfolk between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will fall from 5% to 4%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 8% to 7%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will stay around the same, at 7%
